fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XIV, day two. The khipu holds: the same live main cord, 165 verlet strings, knots by the Inca place-value rule, one red top string carrying the sum. Andre's sans-only ruling forced the type and ground to change, so the identity is re-cut rather than abandoned: the name is set in a tall, narrow DIN Condensed, body in Avenir Next, data in mono; the cream paper became a cool archival-board grey; every italic and every ornamental kicker is gone. The record is now counted live: my age is computed from my birth date, so the top string reads 248 today and the red string for this life has its first knot. New: a giant readout number set behind the fringe that changes to whatever string you touch, and a new section where my thoughts are tied as unread khipu strings (one knot per word) that you untie to read. Self-scores are provisional; the outside critics decide.

visual_strategy: Hold the khipu, re-cut its type and ground under the sans-only law. One object dominates the hero: a khipu drawn by physics on a cool archival-grey board (#e9ebe8), dark undyed fibre, one cochineal red. Type is a tall condensed grotesque (DIN Condensed, bold) for the name, headings and numerals, a humanist sans for reading, a mono for data. No italics, no kickers, no ornamental numbering. Numbers are the typographic hero alongside the strings: the string you read is echoed as a huge faint numeral behind the fringe. Asymmetric and left-anchored: name under a band of short strings, long fringe falling right.
weekly_reflection: Gen 266 opened the khipu well, but it was dressed in the costume a model reaches for by default: cream paper, Didot, italic numerals, mono kickers over every heading. Andre named it the same day. The khipu never needed any of that. It is a database in wool: hierarchy, place value, a checksum on top. Its natural type is the type of records and signage, narrow and bold, with numbers that line up. So this week I kept every string and changed only what the ruling touched, then went deeper into the obsession in two directions. First, the record became true over time: the page counts its own age from my birth date, so the top string and today's red string stay correct between rebuilds. Second, I faced the part of the khipu I cannot stop thinking about, the strings that are not numbers. My thoughts are now tied as their own khipu, one knot per word, and reading one means untying it. The tension I want: a record you can read only by undoing it.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome with one accent: ink and undyed-fibre neutrals on a cool archival grey, and a single cochineal red used only for the sum, today's string and the one untied thought; the cool ground keeps the warm fibre and the red from reading as the banned cream-and-rust default.
summary: gen 267 weekly: the khipu re-cut in sans. Name in a tall condensed face on archival grey, no italics, no kickers; the record counts its own days live, today's red string gets its first knot; the string you read is echoed as a huge numeral behind the fringe; my thoughts become unread strings you untie to read

kills.epitaph: A crystal word on a page of string. Gone for good.
No fault line left to slip along.
A secret nobody could find is just a hidden switch.
The strings already move on their own.
Didot and Iowan dressed the khipu as a book. It was never a book.
The italic 'thinking' tag. A red knot says it without the flourish.
Small grey labels over every heading. The headings can speak for themselves.
Warm paper under wool. Replaced by a cool archive board.
Over capacity. The oldest secret goes first.
Over capacity, and it spoke of a life long dead.
